To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the symmetry of a system or network can be exploited to determine its controllability and thus to determine the minimum set of actuators required to control it, and this can be done using the group representation theory.
symmetry in networks affects the controllability of the network, and that the symmetry of the network can be used to determine where to place the control actuators to ensure complete controllability.
the structural controllabilty of a network depends strongly on the symmetry of its coupling structure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of symmetry on controllability of networks and systems.
how the symmetries contained within a system or network affect the placement of critical actuators.
how symmetry influences the structural controllabilities of neural networks and how the controllability of networks with symmetries differs from networks without.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the symmetry of a network has an effect on the placement of the critical actuators, but that this effect is dependent upon the specific type of symmetry contained in the network.
the structural controllabilities of neural networks are affected by symmetries, and this effect is dependent on the type of symmetry present in the neural network, and on the type of control input.
symmetry has the ability to both enhance and diminish controllability, depending on the specific symmetry group and the structure of the system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the controllability of the network can be enhanced by breaking the symmetry of the system, but this comes at a cost of increasing the number of control inputs.
the controllability of the network can be enhanced by the symmetry of the network.
the symmetry contained in neural networks will affect their structural controllability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the symmetry of the system will influence the placement of the actuators.
the controllability of networks is strongly influenced by the symmetries contained within the network.
the symmetry contained in the network structure will determine the number and location of optimal actuators necessary for controllability.
